detail.text: The remaining hole --h1 is Stroeker–de Weger 1999 Theorem 3 (all integral points of (39), a rank-1 elliptic curve). Its proof is a linear form in elliptic logarithms (David's bound) plus LLL reduction. Nothing in Mathlib formalises integral points on elliptic curves, and no elementary argument is known to me: (39) has real points along an asymptote of irrational slope (the real root of t³ + t² − 1 = 0 governs k/(n−k)), so congruence or size arguments alone do not close it. review.words: Is it true that, for every integer $t\geq1$, there is some integer $a$ such that ${n \choose k} = a$ with $1\leq k \le \frac{n}{2}$ has exactly $t$ solutions?
